body: This button probably needs a more elaborate explanation, but I wasn't sure how to implement it. Make the tooltip more verbose? Show a confirmation dialog?

Maybe you can display where the cyclic reference is? For example display a node path and the export variable name from which this button is going to remove the cyclic reference? Otherwise it's not clear what is going to happen after you click the button.

That would require instantiating the scene and searching all properties. Not very feasible.
The dependencies are determined by `[ext_resource]` tags, it does not hold information of where in the scene they are located exactly.

Thanks very much for picking this up @KoBeWi 

I argued in the earlier PR that I'm not convinced an auto-fix like this is a good idea:

* It has to pick an arbitrary place to break the cycle or make the user pick one
* Since godot users often don't use git or other revision control (lack of native non-plugin IDE integration) this may modify user files that aren't under revision control in a way that may not be obvious to the user or easy to find
* Since godot projects don't often have an extensive test suite, users may inadvertently save the now-nil resource and not notice what it broke until much later.

For those reasons I suggest the UI should tell the user how to fix it, but not fix it for them.

It's also worth noting that this improvement fixes the loading-side of the problem. But users will still get confusing exceptions about nil values where they are visibly not nil if they have just created a reference cycle; godot returns nil instead of the resource to be loaded, rather than throwing a more informative exception. That doesn't need to be solved in the same PR of course, but is worth knowing about.
